whoIsThisFor.heading: Who is the Public Sector Solutions Consultant exam for?

personas.label: Government and public sector consultants
personas.description: You implement agency programs such as permits, inspections, grants, benefits, or case management.

personas.label: Public Sector Solutions AP holders moving up
personas.description: You hold the Public Sector Solutions Accredited Professional credential and want to move into consultant-level delivery.

personas.label: Business Analysts on government projects

examDifficulty.heading: Is the Public Sector Solutions Consultant Exam Hard?
examDifficulty.summary: The exam focuses on designing Public Sector Solutions for agency work. Review licensing, inspections, grants and benefits, case management, and services for constituents.
bullets: Exam fee: US$150; retakes are US$75 through April 27, 2027.
examDifficulty.passRateGuidance: Practice explaining a permitting process, a grant or benefit case, and a self-service application. Identify the Public Sector Solutions records and configuration needed for each.

examFormat.heading: Public Sector Solutions Consultant Exam Format Explained
examFormat.intro: The supervised exam uses multiple-choice and multiple-select questions and can be taken online or at a test center.
examFormat.scenarioPercent: Questions can describe an agency requirement and ask you to choose a setup for licensing, case management, or constituent self-service.
bestWayToPass: Trace a permit: Follow an application through review, approval, renewal, and compliance work.
Review government cases: Match case types, queues, and escalation paths to agency needs.
Study grants and benefits: Connect eligibility decisions, payments, and compliance tracking to the program process.
Design self-service: Explore how constituents can apply, submit documents, and check status using Experience Cloud and guided flows.

expertInsight: Use the official Public Sector Solutions Consultant guide and Trailhead preparation materials to define your study scope. Check the consultant objectives separately from the Accredited Professional material so you cover the required depth.

certificationCard.description: This exam tests your ability to design and implement Public Sector Solutions programs: licensing and permitting, inspections, grants and benefits, case management, and constituent self-service. It has 60 scored questions plus up to five unscored questions, with 105 minutes to complete it. The passing score is 72%.

keyConcepts.h2: Public Sector Solutions Consultant: Key Concepts for the Exam

blocks.heading: Licensing and Permitting
blocks.body: Map licensing and permit applications to the agency’s actual review, approval, renewal and compliance steps. Configure the lifecycle around those requirements.

blocks.heading: Inspections
blocks.body: Connect an inspection to the relevant permit, license or case. Its result can inform later compliance work.

blocks.heading: Grants and Benefits Management
blocks.body: Grant and benefit programs may need eligibility checks, application review, disbursement and reporting. Define rules and records that support consistent decisions and an audit trail.

blocks.heading: Case Management for Government
blocks.body: Design case types, queues and escalation paths around the agency’s regulatory and constituent-service work. Consider service targets and accountability when routing cases.

blocks.heading: Constituent Self-Service
blocks.body: A constituent portal can let residents or businesses submit applications and check their status. Plan the Experience Cloud experience around the services and access each user needs.

scenarioTips.h2: How to Pass the Public Sector Solutions Consultant Exam
scenarioTips.intro: For each agency scenario, first identify the program and its users. Then compare the available configuration against the stated requirement.

blocks.heading: Identify the program type first
blocks.body: First decide whether the requirement concerns a permit, benefit, grant or another service. Then match the proposed configuration to that process.

blocks.heading: Separate inspections from generic case management
blocks.body: If the work involves an inspection, identify the related permit or case and what should happen after the result is recorded.

blocks.heading: Default to self-service when the scenario is about reducing staff workload
blocks.body: For online applications and status checks, assess whether a constituent portal meets the requirement and access needs.

blocks.heading: Watch for compliance and auditability requirements
blocks.body: Look for requirements to document eligibility, approvals and reviews. The process should retain the evidence needed for an audit.

nextCertsAfter.heading: Next Consultant Certifications
nextCertsAfter.intro: After this credential, round out your public sector and consultant track:

sampleQuestions.question: A city agency wants people to renew business licenses online without calling an office. What should it use?
options: Set up a self-service license renewal flow in Experience Cloud.
Require every renewal to be mailed to the agency office.
Ask staff to process each renewal through an internal Chatter post.
Stop accepting renewals, even when a license is still valid.
sampleQuestions.explanation: Experience Cloud can provide a self-service process so people can complete license renewals online.
whyWrong: Mailing renewals does not meet the goal of online self-service.
Chatter is for internal collaboration, not a public renewal process.
The agency needs to support renewals, not disable them.

sampleQuestions.question: An inspection fails for a permitted facility. What should happen next?
options: Treat inspections as informational and take no action on the permit. while following the agency review and access rules
Link the failed inspection to a compliance action on the related permit.
Renew the permit automatically despite the failed inspection.
Delete the inspector’s calendar instead of changing the permit.
sampleQuestions.explanation: Linking inspection results to the permit lets a failure trigger the required compliance action.
whyWrong: A failed inspection can affect compliance; it should not be ignored.
Automatic renewal despite failure would defeat the purpose of the inspection.
Calendar settings do not determine how the agency handles an inspection result.

sampleQuestions.question: A grants program must check income and residency before approving payment. What does this describe?
options: Case escalation for urgent constituent issues.
Scheduling inspections at applicant addresses.
Grant eligibility and compliance tracking.
Changing the visual theme of the public website.
sampleQuestions.explanation: Checking income and residency before payment is part of grants and benefits eligibility and compliance.
whyWrong: Case escalation routes urgent cases; it does not decide grant eligibility.
Inspection scheduling is separate from reviewing income and residency.
Website theming is cosmetic and does not check eligibility.

sampleQuestions.question: A pothole complaint should be escalated if it remains unresolved after five business days. What should the consultant configure?
options: A report that staff may review when they have time.
A permanent lock that prevents staff from updating the case.
A reminder that relies on the agent to remember the deadline.
A case escalation rule or SLA flow tied to the case queue.
sampleQuestions.explanation: A case escalation rule or SLA-based flow can trigger action when the five-day deadline is reached.
whyWrong: A report does not trigger an escalation by itself.
Locking the case stops staff from resolving it.
A manual reminder is easy to miss and does not enforce the service target.

sampleQuestions.question: How do the Public Sector Solutions AP and Consultant exams differ?
options: The AP covers basics; the Consultant exam covers full implementation.
They are the same exam offered under two different names.
The Consultant exam has no connection to Public Sector Solutions. while following the agency review and access rules
The AP replaced the Consultant exam and is no longer separate.
sampleQuestions.explanation: The AP focuses on foundational setup. The Consultant exam tests deeper implementation across programs such as licensing, grants, and case management.
whyWrong: These are separate credentials with different levels of coverage.
The Consultant exam is specifically about Public Sector Solutions implementation.
Both credentials are distinct exams; the AP did not replace the Consultant exam.

sampleQuestions.question: Applicants must upload proof of residency and income with an online application. What should the consultant recommend?
options: Require applicants to fax each document to the agency.
Add file uploads to the Experience Cloud application flow.
Turn off attachments across Salesforce so no files can be submitted.
Ask applicants to print and mail every supporting document.
sampleQuestions.explanation: A document upload step in the online application keeps submission self-service and reduces manual intake.
whyWrong: Faxing documents does not meet the goal of an online application.
Turning off attachments prevents applicants from submitting the required evidence.
Mailing printed documents does not meet the goal of online self-service.

sampleQuestions.question: A licensing board needs different approval steps for first-time applications and renewals. What is the best design?
options: Use one identical approval path for every license request.
Reject every renewal automatically, regardless of its details.
Use separate lifecycle paths for new applications and renewals.
Ask board members to remember which steps apply to each request.
sampleQuestions.explanation: Separate lifecycle paths or record types let the system apply the right approval steps to each application type.
whyWrong: One identical path would ignore the different approval requirements.
Automatically rejecting all renewals would prevent valid renewals.
Relying on memory is less reliable than configuring the process in Salesforce.

sampleQuestions.question: Which request is mainly about case management rather than licensing, grants, or inspections?
options: Track a business permit’s annual renewal date. while following the agency review and access rules
Check a grant applicant’s household income before payment. while following the agency review and access rules
Schedule a routine inspection for a permitted facility.
Route and resolve a complaint through queues and deadlines.
sampleQuestions.explanation: Routing and resolving a constituent complaint through queues and service deadlines is case management.
whyWrong: Permit renewal is a licensing and permitting task.
Checking income for a grant is a grants and benefits task.
Scheduling a facility inspection is an inspection-management task.

sampleQuestions.question: Legal staff need a complete audit trail of every benefit eligibility decision that cannot be changed afterward. What should the consultant ensure?
options: Store each decision and its evidence in a protected system of record.
Keep decisions only in an employee’s private notes outside the case record.
Delete the decision details after approval to reduce storage use.
Allow any user to change an eligibility decision at any time.
sampleQuestions.explanation: The system of record should capture each decision and supporting data and protect it from unauthorized changes.
whyWrong: Private notes do not provide a complete audit trail in the system of record.
Deleting decision details would remove the audit history.
Unrestricted edits would undermine the audit trail’s integrity.

sampleQuestions.question: A constituent sees “Under Review” when checking a benefits application online. What should supply that status?
options: A fixed image that never changes as the case moves forward.
The status on the actual case or application record, shown in the portal.
A randomly selected status that is separate from the agency record. while following the agency review and access rules
A personal email the constituent sent to themselves. while following the agency review and access rules
sampleQuestions.explanation: The portal should display the current status stored on the related case or application record.
whyWrong: A fixed image cannot show changes to the application.
A random status would not reflect the application’s real state.
The constituent’s own email is not connected to the agency record.

sampleQuestions.question: Why is constituent self-service useful when designing a public program?
options: It leaves agency staff workload unchanged.
It applies only to private-sector businesses.
Self-service cuts intake work and shows status.
It removes the need for case management altogether.
sampleQuestions.explanation: Self-service reduces manual intake and gives constituents a way to submit requests and check their status.
whyWrong: Self-service is intended to reduce some manual work for staff.
Public agencies use self-service for public programs.
Self-service works alongside case management; it does not replace it.

sampleQuestions.question: An inspector should see only inspections assigned to their territory. What should control this access?
options: The agency’s available Salesforce storage space.
The inspector’s email signature and contact details.
The color theme on the Lightning page. while following the agency review and access rules
Record-level sharing by territory or assignment.
sampleQuestions.explanation: Record-level sharing and visibility settings can limit inspection records based on territory or assignment.
whyWrong: Storage limits affect capacity, not which records a user can view.
Email signatures do not control record access.
Page color is cosmetic and does not affect data access.

sampleQuestions.question: A grants program wants missing documents flagged before an application reaches a reviewer. What should it use?
options: Use validation or Flow to flag missing documents.
A manual review with no automatic checks or alerts.
Automatic approval of every application, even when documents are missing.
Automatic rejection of every application without reviewing it.
sampleQuestions.explanation: Validation or Flow logic can identify missing documents before the application reaches a reviewer.
whyWrong: Manual-only review does not meet the requirement to flag missing items automatically.
Approving incomplete applications ignores the stated requirement.
The agency wants to flag incomplete applications for review, not reject every application.

sampleQuestions.question: What does licensing and permitting configuration in Public Sector Solutions support?
options: One fixed application process for every type of license. while following the agency review and access rules
A configurable application-to-compliance lifecycle for each permit type.
A process that has no connection to inspections or compliance. while following the agency review and access rules
A system that only federal agencies can use. while following the agency review and access rules
sampleQuestions.explanation: Licensing and permitting tools support a configurable lifecycle for each license or permit type, including review, renewal, and compliance.
whyWrong: Agencies can configure processes for different license types.
Licensing and permitting can connect to inspections and compliance.
Public Sector Solutions supports public agencies at different levels of government.

sampleQuestions.question: A city agency investigates fraud across departments and needs to share relevant case details with an authorized partner. What should the consultant recommend?
options: Publish the full case file on a public portal while following the agency review and access rules
Email all case records to every partner employee
Use Investigative Case Management with need-to-know sharing
Copy restricted details into an unrestricted spreadsheet while following the agency review and access rules
sampleQuestions.explanation: Investigative Case Management supports investigation workflows, while compliant sharing should limit disclosure to authorized recipients and relevant data.
whyWrong: Publishing a full file would expose case details broadly.
Sending all records ignores authorization and data minimization.
An unrestricted spreadsheet can expose sensitive details outside approved controls.

sampleQuestions.question: An agency wants investigators to manage complex matters involving people, incidents, evidence, and follow-up. Which solution is most relevant?
options: Licensing and permit renewal while following the agency review and access rules
Investigative Case Management
Volunteer shift scheduling
Donor gift servicing while following the agency review and access rules
sampleQuestions.explanation: Investigative Case Management supports investigation workflows and related records such as people, incidents, evidence, and activities.
whyWrong: Licensing handles permits and renewals, not investigations.
Volunteer scheduling is unrelated to public-sector investigations.
Donor gift servicing is a nonprofit fundraising workflow.

sampleQuestions.question: An investigator needs to share case information with another authorized agency while protecting restricted details. What should the consultant recommend?
options: Export the full case file to a public folder while following the agency review and access rules
Email all records to every partner contact while following the agency review and access rules
Use approved, permission-controlled sharing and disclose only authorized data
Copy sensitive details into an unrestricted report while following the agency review and access rules
sampleQuestions.explanation: Use compliant sharing controls, confirm recipient authorization, and disclose only the information needed for the permitted purpose.
whyWrong: This alternative does not meet the scenario requirements. Use compliant sharing controls, confirm recipient authorization, and disclose only the information needed for the permitted purpose.
This alternative does not meet the scenario requirements. Use compliant sharing controls, confirm recipient authorization, and disclose only the information needed for the permitted purpose.
This alternative does not meet the scenario requirements. Use compliant sharing controls, confirm recipient authorization, and disclose only the information needed for the permitted purpose.

sampleQuestions.question: A licensing team wants applicants to submit complete applications online and check progress. What should the portal support?
options: Staff-only access with no status view while following the agency review and access rules
A shared spreadsheet of applicant data while following the agency review and access rules
A generic page that accepts no documents while following the agency review and access rules
Secure submission, required document collection, and application status
sampleQuestions.explanation: A secure self-service experience can collect required materials and show relevant case or application status.
whyWrong: A staff-only process does not provide online applicant self-service.
A shared spreadsheet creates access and process-control risks.
A page that cannot accept documents does not meet the stated requirement.

sampleQuestions.question: A benefits program needs to verify eligibility before a caseworker approves an application. What should the process include?
options: Configured eligibility checks and a review step before determination
Automatic approval of every submitted application while following the agency review and access rules
A permit inspection with no applicant record while following the agency review and access rules
A public report containing income documents while following the agency review and access rules
sampleQuestions.explanation: Eligibility rules and review steps help staff assess an application before making a benefits determination.
whyWrong: Automatic approval skips the required eligibility assessment.
A permit inspection is a different public-sector workflow.
Sensitive documents should not be exposed through a public report.

sampleQuestions.question: A field inspector completes a site visit and finds a violation. What should happen next?
options: Delete the inspection record while following the agency review and access rules
Replace the inspection with a grant application while following the agency review and access rules
Close the matter without notifying staff while following the agency review and access rules
Record findings and route the case for the required follow-up
sampleQuestions.explanation: Recording findings and routing follow-up preserves the inspection history and supports enforcement or remediation.
whyWrong: This alternative does not meet the scenario requirements. Recording findings and routing follow-up preserves the inspection history and supports enforcement or remediation.
